scope: segment checksum vs unreadable — the two failure kinds
statement: a READABLE-but-corrupt segment (checksum/magic/decompress failure) still salvages decompressable lines and records a quarantine skip — partial truth, recorded — while an UNREADABLE segment throws: nothing can be known about it, so nothing can be honestly salvaged. Two different answers to two genuinely different questions

deliberately lenient after RULING-54, each with its reason in place: the app-fringe readers (search content, background word-count stats, closed-doc task derivation, the rename pre-check, the statement-preview classifier, the scenes sidebar, the project task log) read via try? and SKIP an unreadable doc — every one of them meets the loud refusal the moment the doc is opened, and none can mutate anything from the shortened view. The queue is EMPTY as of 2026-08-12: checkpoints closed (M9-OL-007/008), then the residual family (M9-OL-009 publications, M9-OL-010 pending buffer, M9-OL-011 backup signature, M9-OL-012 the seal's recorded reason). The recorded-lenient set now also carries the two dev-only checkpoint test tools and sealTailIfNeeded's skip

scope: the checkpoint surfaces — HistoryPane notice, ProjectIntegrity finding, backup gate
statement: the unreadable checkpoint files reach the writer: the History pane shows a notice naming them with the per-file reasons in its tooltip (the inbox pane's M8-IN-012 shape; copy pinned via the static HistoryPane.unreadableCheckpointNotice/unreadableCheckpointDetail), ProjectIntegrity reports them as findings — isHealthy false — instead of FEWER findings (an unreadable file used to shrink the checkpoint set through try? … ?? [] and with it the dangling-pointer check, so the report got healthier exactly when the project got worse), and the two dev-only checkpoint test tools carry an `unreadable` field so a broken fixture fails loudly instead of skewing a count. The backup gate deliberately does NOT block on this finding (whole-branch review finding A): IntegrityReport.blocksBackup is the manuscript-derived four only, because the realistic causes of an unreadable checkpoint file (another device's iCloud dataless stub while offline, a permissions break) are exactly the moments a backup matters most, and refusing to back up the writer's words over a non-manuscript index would invert constitution must #1 — manuscript-derived corruption still blocks, because it would propagate into every generation
reachability: LIVE — the History pane's every reload; every integrity check; every backup

statement: a pending file that EXISTS but cannot be read or decoded holds the writer's un-bursted keystrokes from a crashed session; it used to collapse into the absent case (silent return) and the next autosave's flushToDisk overwrote the only copy. loadFromDisk now reports absent / loaded / unrecoverable(name, reason, raw — the bytes when readable); Document.load quarantines the salvageable bytes under .maugham/conflicts/quarantine BEFORE that overwrite can happen, then STAMPS the failure on the Document (consume-once) — it does not post the notice itself, because a windowless post is dropped by the receive helpers' liveness guard (isLive(nil) == false) and a clean close then deletes the trigger: the forbidden silence, relocated (whole-branch review finding C). EditorHost consumes the stamp and posts when a window exists, with BOTH triggers (load-completion and window-resolution — either can happen first). A notice, not a refusal: every SAVED word is intact in the op log (fix 9772aea2 + the review's delivery fix)
reachability: LIVE — every document open after a crash

scope: BackupSignature.compute — unreadable file in the change-detection hash
statement: an UNREADABLE-yet-present file contributes a distinct '<rel>\tunreadable' marker line to the backup signature, never silence — dropping it made the signature EQUAL to the file-deleted state (RED-watched against the old code, 2026-08-12), so change detection could not tell 'became unreadable' from 'was removed' and a skip-unchanged verdict could stand on a state it never actually hashed. Deterministic across calls. The WRITE path was already loud (copyItem throws on the unreadable file → .failed per destination); this closes the read half (fix commit 9772aea2)
reachability: LIVE — every backup run's change detection
